audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate strings credit Fury of the Sands with lifesteal: content mid "my Fury of the Sands hands me lifesteal, size and bonus resists", content late "R gives me lifesteal and bonus resists", spikes[3].text "R's lifesteal, size and bonus resists".
audit.why: Fury of the Sands grants bonus Health, bonus Attack Range, an area damage aura, a reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown and bonus Armor and Magic Resist. The lifesteal in this kit comes from Soul Eater, the passive, and it is available from level 1 — a player who thinks R is what heals him will hold his ultimate for sustain he already has.
audit.corrected: Rewrote all three to bonus health, reach and resists, and named Soul Eater as the source of the healing.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json (P Soul Eater: bonus Life Steal; R Fury of the Sands: increased Health, Attack Range, reduced Q cooldown, bonus Armor and Magic Resistance)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] says to stack "behind the minion line" but never says why that works, so it reads as generic safety advice rather than a hard counter to his main damage.
audit.why: Shock Blast detonates on the first enemy it hits. A single minion between Nasus and the orb eats the entire poke pattern this lane is built on. That is the difference between conceding levels 1-3 and taking almost nothing.
audit.corrected: Stated the detonate-on-first-unit rule in wants.you[1], content early, breakdown.cooldowns and breakdown.mid.
sources: champ-data/_kits/jayce.json (Q Shock Blast: "Fires an orb of electricity that detonates upon hitting an enemy (or reaching the end of its path)")

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry treats Acceleration Gate as a passive fact of levels 2-3 rather than as a visible tell.
audit.why: A Shock Blast fired through the gate gains missile speed, range and damage. The gate is placed first and is visible on the ground, so it is a free half-second of warning before the biggest poke in the matchup — the sidestep cue is the gate, not the orb.
audit.corrected: Made the gate the explicit dodge cue in content early and whys[1].
sources: champ-data/_kits/jayce.json (E Acceleration Gate: "If Shock Blast is fired through the gate the missile speed, range, and damage will increase")

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns lists Shock Blast twice — once as "Jayce Shock Blast" and again as "Jayce To the Skies! / Shock Blast" — with no numbers on either.
audit.why: The duplicate wastes the only place a player looks for timings. Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1 falling to 6s, and Thundering Blow is 20s at rank 1 with only 240 range. Wither reaches 700, so Nasus can land his slow from well outside the range at which Jayce can knock him off a wave — that range gap is the whole mid-lane pattern and it appeared nowhere.
audit.corrected: Replaced the duplicate with Thundering Blow and put the real ranges and cooldowns on both.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] explains why Wither beats his kiting but not why it beats his damage.
audit.why: Hyper Charge, the cannon W, grants maximum Attack Speed for a few attacks. Wither decays attack speed, so the slow lands on the one buff he was counting on to burst a melee down. Also removed "halves his move and attack speed" — the actual slow percentages are not in the kit files and I could not verify that fraction.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text now leads with the 700-vs-240 range gap; content mid names Hyper Charge as what the slow eats.
sources: champ-data/_kits/jayce.json (W Hyper Charge: "increasing Attack Speed to maximum for several attacks")
champ-data/_kits/nasus.json (W Wither decelerates Move Speed and Attack Speed)

edits.before: - Jayce Shock Blast: matchup-defining — His main poke. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Jayce To the Skies! / Shock Blast: Hammer: leap + slow. Cannon: a long-range artillery line. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Jayce Shock Blast: matchup-defining — 16s at rank 1, 6s maxed, detonating on the first thing it touches, so hold the minion line. - Jayce Thundering Blow: 240-range knockback, 20s at rank 1 — Wither reaches 700.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Shock Blast: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If ahead, freeze and starve him.
edits.after: Trade strictly around Shock Blast: it detonates on the first unit it touches, so keep a minion between you and him. If ahead, freeze and starve him.

edits.before: My W Wither halves his move and attack speed, killing the Hextech Capacitor swap-speed he kites with and dragging him into a melee trade his squishy frame loses.
edits.after: My W Wither lands from 700 range, well outside Thundering Blow's 240, and it guts the Capacitor swap speed that kites me plus the Hyper Charge burst.

edits.after: Hundreds of Q stacks plus R's bonus health, reach and resists mean one Wither pins Jayce in melee while a single empowered Q chunks his low-HP frame.

edits.before: Stack Q safely behind the minion line, soaking XP while my Spirit Fire shreds his armor and Soul Eater heals his poke off

edits.before: His E unlocks Acceleration Gate, so Shock Blast becomes a long-range gated orb and the cannon swap shreds my Armor as I step up to stack Q, handing him a free trade.
edits.after: His E unlocks Acceleration Gate, and a Shock Blast fired through it gains speed, range and damage while the cannon swap shreds my Armor as I step up.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 belong to Jayce and I just have to eat it. At Level 1 he only has one Cannon-Q, so I soak my Q farm and accept the poke while we're both weak. It gets worse at 2-3 when his E Acceleration Gate unlocks: a gated Shock Blast chunks me at full range, and his first hit after a cannon-to-hammer swap shreds my Armor every single time I walk up for a stack. Don't overcommit to a stack on a freezing wave or his E Thundering Blow knocks me off it and I lose the stack AND the XP. Last-hit with the tip of Q, take the poke, and trust that Soul Eater heals it.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 belong to Jayce and I just have to eat it. At Level 1 he only has one Cannon-Q, so I soak my Q farm and accept the poke while we're both weak. It gets worse at 2-3 when his E Acceleration Gate unlocks: a Shock Blast fired through the gate gains speed, range and damage, so the gate hitting the ground IS the tell — sidestep the moment you see it, and keep a minion in the way because the orb detonates on the first thing it touches. Don't overcommit to a stack on a freezing wave or his E Thundering Blow knocks me off it and I lose the stack AND the XP.

edits.before: This is where I claw it back to even, so I trade smart around W. By Levels 4-5 I have a real stack count and Wither, and the second that slow lands his Hextech Capacitor swap speed is useless and he's stuck in a melee fight his squishy frame loses. So I only let him commit the gate-Q into swap into Hammer combo while my Wither is on cooldown, and I punish hard the moment he's in range with the slow up. Level 6 is a flat spot for him because his R is just the stance-swap he already had, while my Fury of the Sands hands me lifesteal, size and bonus resists, so this is where the lane stops being his.
edits.after: This is where I claw it back to even, so I trade smart around W. So I only let him commit the gate-Q into swap into Hammer combo while my Wither is on cooldown, and I punish hard the moment he's in range with the slow up. Level 6 is a flat spot for him because his R is just the stance-swap he already had, while my Fury of the Sands hands me bonus health, reach and resists, so this is where the lane stops being his.

edits.before: Late game is mine because I'm a hard scaler and Jayce isn't. A free-farmed Nasus reaches hundreds of Q stacks, R gives me lifesteal and bonus resists, and one Wither pins Jayce in melee while a single empowered Q chunks his low-HP frame. He can't out-duel that head-on. The whole job in the early game was just to survive his poke without feeding a snowball, and Spirit Fire's armor shred plus Soul Eater make that doable. If I farmed even, I win every extended fight and become the splitpush threat he can't answer alone.

notes: suspectNames flagged "Spirit Fire's" in content late — false positive, that is Nasus's own E with a possessive apostrophe. Removed an unverifiable number: spikes[1].text claimed Wither "halves his move and attack speed"; Wither's actual slow percentages and its ramp are not in the kit files, so I replaced the fraction with the 700-vs-240 range fact, which is verifiable. Left one claim I could not check either way: content mid says Jayce's level 6 is a flat spot "because his R is just the stance-swap he already had". Whether Jayce's Transform is available before level 6 is not answerable from the kit file, so I preserved the existing wording verbatim rather than build new text on top of it — worth a check on the Wiki, because if it is wrong then level 6 is being sold as a free window that isn't one.
